ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Postural symptoms

A 59-year-old woman taking imipramine becomes lightheaded when standing. Blood pressure falls from 132/78 mm Hg supine to 102/64 mm Hg upright. She has no bleeding, vomiting or diarrhea. Which action of imipramine most directly impairs the normal vascular response to standing?

  1. Fast sodium-channel blockade in ventricular tissue
  2. Peripheral alpha-1 receptor blockade
  3. Histamine H1 receptor blockade
  4. Muscarinic receptor blockade
  5. Serotonin transporter blockade
Answer and explanation

Peripheral alpha-1 receptor blockade

Reduced arteriolar and venous constriction contributes to orthostatic hypotension.

Option explanations

Peripheral alpha-1 receptor blockade: Reduced arteriolar and venous constriction contributes to orthostatic hypotension.

Histamine H1 receptor blockade: This contributes to sleepiness but does not chiefly explain the impaired postural vasoconstriction.

Muscarinic receptor blockade: This explains anticholinergic effects and tachycardia rather than the main vascular defect.

Serotonin transporter blockade: This is not the most direct explanation of the orthostatic vascular response.

Fast sodium-channel blockade in ventricular tissue: This is important in cardiotoxicity but is not the best explanation of isolated postural hypotension.
